blocks.text: Setting up your Notion workspace on Mac

Start by installing the official Notion desktop app. Ensure you are running macOS 13 or later to avoid compatibility issues. Once installed, use the Notion menu in the top bar to check for updates regularly. This keeps your interface snappy and ensures you have the latest features for your tutoring business.

Organize your workspace with a top-level page called Tutoring Hub. Inside this page, create a database for your students. Add properties for their email, current level, and next session date. This gives you a clear view of your entire practice at a glance.

Stop creating every lesson plan from scratch. Create a database template for your lesson notes. Include sections for learning objectives, resources, and homework assignments. When you start a new session, click the arrow next to the New button in your database and select your template. This saves you valuable minutes before every call.
Use the /toggle command to hide detailed lesson notes. This keeps your page clean while teaching, but lets you expand sections when you need to check specific details during a session.
blocks.title: Keep your view clean

blocks.text: Using keyboard shortcuts for faster navigation

Speed is critical when you are live on a call with a student. Learn these essential shortcuts to work faster on your Mac. Press Cmd + P to open the search bar and jump to any student page instantly. Use Cmd + N to create a new page in your current location. Type / to open the block menu and quickly add text, images, or databases.

Create a linked database view for each student. Filter this view to show only entries related to that specific student. This prevents your main dashboard from becoming cluttered. You can also add a formula property to calculate the number of sessions completed. This is a great way to track billing cycles or progress milestones.

Many tutors store materials in Google Drive or Canva. You can embed these directly into Notion pages. Use the /embed command to link your Google Sheets for grading or your Canva decks for lessons. This keeps all your teaching assets accessible without leaving Notion.
Common mistakes tutors make in Notion

items: Over-complicating the workspace with too many nested pages.
Failing to use templates for repetitive tasks like session notes.
Not setting up proper database filters, leading to information overload.
Ignoring the desktop app in favor of the browser, which can be slower on Mac.
Leaving sensitive student data unprotected by not using page locks.

faq.question: Can I use Notion for free as a tutor?
faq.answer: Yes, Notion offers a free plan for individuals that is perfect for solo tutors. You can create unlimited pages and blocks in your workspace.

faq.question: How do I make Notion faster on my Mac?
faq.answer: Use the dedicated desktop app instead of a browser tab. Press Cmd + R to reload the app if it feels sluggish, and keep your pages lightweight by avoiding excessive high-resolution images.
